title: L-fucose in WWOX research
summary: Retain as a conditional salvage-pathway probe. Defer pediatric WWOX trial priority until a native glycan deficit and its circuit response are measured.

graph.evidence: Free fucose, GDP-fucose and protein fucosylation can diverge.
graph.inference: CSF exposure alone cannot verify correction of a neural glycosite.
graph.hypothesis: Salvage may correct a selected GluA2 site and independently change release.
graph.experiment: Measure labeled donor, GluA2 core fucose and early release at matched exposure.

evidence: In one GLUT1 deficiency report, free CSF fucose rose to about 31 µM. Overall CSF lectin staining moved toward reference. A predominantly CNS-derived protein remained hypofucosylated.
In Fut8 heterozygous mice, brain GDP-fucose reached about 1.34 times the WT signal, while the selected hippocampal mono-core-fucosylation index recovered about 20% of its deficit.
inference: Measure local free fucose, the labeled donor and absolute site occupancy separately. A rapid rise in mouse hippocampal excitatory release makes a functional control necessary.
hypothesis: If deficient WWOX GluA2 core fucosylation is substrate responsive, correction should follow recovery of the donor and alter the delayed postsynaptic response.
experiment: Verify a baseline site deficit, then compare matched WWOX and control preparations on exposure, early release, the corrected glycopeptide and late network activity. A rise in early release or recurrence lowers priority.
limits: The human CSF report describes one case with another disease. Brain interstitial exposure, target response and pediatric safety remain undetermined in WWOX.
